summary: The article argues that the College Football Playoff committee's decision to leave unbeaten ACC champion Florida State out of the final four-team field exposed college football's identity crisis: whether the playoff should reward the best or the most deserving teams. The committee chose Michigan, Washington, Texas and Alabama, preferring Alabama despite its loss to Texas. The author contends Florida State was robbed and that the decision undermines the importance of regular-season results ahead of the 12-team expansion in 2024.
one_line: The CFP committee excluded unbeaten Florida State from the final four-team playoff, which the author says shows the sport values looks over results.
key_facts: Florida State became the first unbeaten Power 5 conference champion left out of the College Football Playoff field.
The final four-team CFP field was 1. Michigan, 2. Washington, 3. Texas, 4. Alabama.
The 2023 season is the last of the four-team era; the CFP expands to 12 teams in 2024.
Florida State beat Louisville 16-6 in the ACC Championship Game with a third-string quarterback after Jordan Travis broke his leg two weeks earlier.
Alabama, a one-loss SEC champion, beat Georgia on Saturday, ending the Bulldogs' 29-game winning streak.
Texas, a one-loss Big 12 champion, beat Alabama by 10 points in Tuscaloosa in September.
Texas's only loss came in a nail-biter in its rivalry game against Oklahoma.
Ohio State won the national title in the inaugural four-team season with a third-string quarterback, after winning the Big Ten title game 59-0.
CFP committee chair Boo Corrigan said of Florida State: 'You look at who they are as a team without Jordan Travis — they are a different team.'
Florida State coach Mike Norvell said he was 'disgusted and infuriated' and asked, 'What is the point of playing games?'
Jordan Travis tweeted he was 'devastated. heartbroken.' and said 'I thought results matter. 13-0'.
The author says the right move would have been to leave Alabama out, and notes the committee decision was made by thirteen people in a hotel boardroom in Grapevine, Texas.
